audio_caption: The audio clip starts with enthusiastic cheers and applause. Upbeat rock music with a clear driving beat takes over, featuring electric guitars and a strong drum line. A male voice then compliments a woman saying, "You look sensational. Just sensational, well done with your thing and all that." The tone is friendly and appreciative. He then notes, "It's lovely, I like your earrings too." The woman responds, sounding appreciative, "Thank you. I'm not sure, they're just some fun little, very different than the Vikings." The man agrees, saying "Yes," then immediately congratulates someone on "the Vikings."

The audio clip begins with two speakers, a man and a woman, discussing a popular television show. The man notes it's the "top-rated show on television" and shares statistics. The woman confirms the numbers. The man finds it "crazy" that "more people watch Vikings than American Idol". He then jokingly states, "screw American Idol. We want large women fighting". At the very end of the clip is a loud and clear audible "thump" sound, with the potential of being the result of a fall or a heavy collision of some sort.

The clip begins with excited male voices, one saying "Kick-ass women."  followed by some laughter.  The interviewer, also male, asks a guest if she engages in "Haa-chaa!" and "Kick-ass".  She responds, describing her martial arts background from age seven, earning a black belt at thirteen, and starting her own school at sixteen. The interviewer then asks if men are "intimidated or strangely attracted to your kick-ass abilities," eliciting laughter from the guest and the interviewer. The interviewer clarifies, finding it "strangely intimidating" yet intriguing. The female guest remarks, "it's one of those things most people don't expect" as she describes looking for a role to show off her martial arts. The clip concludes with the interviewer saying "Yes".

The clip begins with a female speaker recalling a night when she was teaching taekwondo, preparing her students for their black belts. She then mentions going to an ATM in a strip mall in Toronto, which she describes as not the best part of town. A male speaker humorously chimes in, exclaiming "Toronto! It's like a jungle up there!" Following his remark, a brief interlude of upbeat acoustic guitar music plays. The female speaker affirms Toronto's reputation, while the male speaker shifts to complimenting a leg movement of the female speaker, implying her expertise. The female speaker then acknowledges this. The male speaker then makes the final comment asking if "these Canadians jumped you".

The audio begins with a female speaker recounting a startling incident at an ATM, describing how someone ran towards her, grabbed her, and then her name was called by friends. The speaker's tone is initially dramatic and builds to a more conversational tone as the story unfolds. A male voice then responds, questioning the behavior of her friends with a skeptical tone. The female speaker agrees, then the male voice suggests the person should have yelled like a kick-ass. The male voice begins to demonstrate the yell. This causes a mixed reaction from the audience. They then discuss that someone should not run up to people like that.

The audio clip starts with a female speaker discussing the show "Vikings," stating that it's "based on a real character." She adds that the show's creator, Michael Hirst, also made "Tudors" and wrote "Elizabeth." The speaker emphasizes that Hirst worked with a historian to ensure the show's accuracy. During this discussion, the female speaker speaks conversationally with slight emphasis. The clip opens abruptly with a "really?" being stated in an incredulous tone, potentially as a response to the assertion that Vikings is based on a real character.

The audio features two speakers, one male and one female, discussing a character named Lagertha. The woman describes her as "a real kick-ass woman who can actually fight" and explains that she is a "real shield-maiden" who is strong and goes to battle with men. The man expresses surprise that Lagertha is a real person.

The audio clip begins with two individuals, one male and one female, discussing female warriors in the Dark Ages, with the male expressing surprise and enthusiasm about Viking ships carrying both men and women. He admires this and jokingly mentions his own people likely being "pushed around" by the Vikings. The woman gently reminds him that he is from Scotland, confirming their location. The audio ends with them specifying they were shooting in Ireland. The mood is jovial and conversational, punctuated by the male's animated remarks.

A woman states that she is "from born and raised in Toronto, Canada, but my heritage is Ukrainian." A man replies, claiming to know about Ukraine but questions the term "Toronto, Canada." He then asks something in Ukrainian, followed by what sounds like a randomly made-up phrase in a mock Ukrainian accent. The woman speaks at length in Ukrainian, complimenting his nice hair, and saying she could kill him now. The man laughs, stating he doesn't care what she says, doesn't want to know what she means because it means a lot to him, and compliments her talk show skills. There's sparse audience laughter throughout the exchange.

A woman expresses that this is her first time doing something, as a man asks, "You're kidding me." The woman enthusiastically says, "I'm popping my," before a burst of audience laughter and clapping erupts. Someone nervously remarks, "Very nerve wracking." A man quips, "Air conditioning fixed now, right?" This leads to more audience laughter. Someone responds, "Well, good for you then." The laughter continues. The conversation shifts as someone asks if they go back to the Ukraine a lot. The speaker explains they haven't had a chance to go there yet. The conversation continues to discuss the Vikings, as the person states, "Vikings actually invaded Ukraine." There is a discussion about the Vikings being the first navigators. Someone agrees. The speaker continues the conversation. They move onto talking about Viking history, noting that the first Viking King is played by an actor, and remarking that he goes all over to the West. A person jests, "He probably went to Toronto," to which the speaker agrees. They joke about him being in the very strip mall that one speaker was in and that he could have killed those guys. The clip concludes with, "We're out of time."

The clip opens with a male speaker praising someone's performance, followed by an abrupt interjection from another male speaker to "stop applauding" in a joking manner. The first male speaker continues, and the second makes a comment with a playful tone about something "Ukrainian" being ruined. A female speaker then playfully offers to repeat it later. This transitions into a conversation between the two speakers discussing activities like throwing frisbees at a horse and playing the mouth organ. The female speaker chooses the mouth organ. There's a brief exchange about a "weird thing" and an offer to play the mouth organ again. After this, there's a quick exchange with the male speaker saying we're going to commercial break. Finally, there is upbeat instrumental music, likely related to the commercial break.
